topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and the Stolen Necklace Problem
target_audience: Undergraduate students in mathematics or computer science

sections.title: Intuitive Prerequisite: The Antipodal Mapping
lecture_lines: Consider a sphere, the surface S².
They sit exactly opposite each other.
animations: Draw [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] in #FFFFFF. Label 'S²' in #00FF00.
Mark a point 'x' in #FF0000 on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Mark the antipodal point '-x' in #0000FF opposite 'x' on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Connect 'x' and '-x' with a dashed line through center of the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg].
Flash 'x' and '-x' on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg] to emphasize they are antipodal.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
lecture_lines: Any continuous function maps some antipodal pair.
Think of temperature on Earth's surface.
animations: Show a globe [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg] with a temperature gradient in #FFFF00.
Identify antipodal points P1 and P2 on the globe [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg].
Display two identical thermometers [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/thermometer.svg] showing same value in #FF0000.
Show the Borsuk-Ulam theorem text: 'f(x) = f(-x)'.
Highlight the points P1, P2 moving across the globe [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/globe.svg] surface.

sections.title: Transition: The Necklace Problem
lecture_lines: Thieves must divide a beaded necklace.
Each needs half of every bead type.
This is the discrete necklace problem.
animations: Draw a string of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beads.svg] with 10 red (in #FF0000) and 10 blue (in #0000FF).
Draw two separate piles for Thief A and Thief B.
Animate cutting the string at two random points.
Show redistribution of segments into the two piles.
Final state: each pile has 5 red and 5 blue, represented as a completed [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg].

sections.title: The Mathematical Bridge
lecture_lines: We map discrete cuts to a sphere.
Fair division becomes a zero-sum function.
Borsuk-Ulam guarantees an exact fair solution.
animations: Show the necklace [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg] string transforming into a circular loop.
Map the loop onto the surface of a 2D sphere.
Identify cut configurations as coordinates (x, y, z) on sphere.
Visualize the function value crossing zero as the cuts shift.
Highlight the intersection point as the fair division solution using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/necklace.svg] as a reference.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Topology solves complex resource sharing problems.
Curvature of space ensures perfect fairness.
animations: Draw the final balanced piles: 5 red/5 blue in each.
Show Alice and Bob [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/people.svg] smiling, representing fair distribution.
Flash the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scissors.svg] icon as the tool for division.
Overlay: 'Fair division is mathematically guaranteed'.
Fade everything out slowly to black (#000000).
